Name: Stardew Anti-Cheat
Author: Olwtelet
Description:
🛡️ Stardew Anti-Cheat
[b]Stardew Anti-Cheat[/b] is a host-authoritative anti-cheat system designed for Stardew Valley co-op multiplayer.
Instead of relying only on what a player's client reports, the mod combines [b]cooperative mod verification[/b] with [b]host-side behavioral validation[/b]. The host monitors synchronized game state for suspicious or impossible changes involving money, inventory, movement, energy, progression, combat and world activity.
The goal is not to claim that cheating can be made impossible. Stardew Valley was not designed around a competitive server-authoritative architecture. Instead, Stardew Anti-Cheat is designed to make casual cheating significantly harder, provide useful evidence to the host, and give private multiplayer servers much better control over what happens on their farm.
[line]
[heading]✨ Main Features[/heading]
🛡️ Host-Authoritative Monitoring
Important player data is monitored from the host using Stardew Valley's synchronized multiplayer state.
The anti-cheat can detect suspicious behavior involving:
[list]
[*]Unexpected money increases[/*]
[*]Impossible or unusually valuable inventory gains[/*]
[*]Item stacks exceeding normal limits[/*]
[*]Excessive movement speed[/*]
[*]Impossible energy values[/*]
[*]Suspicious energy regeneration[/*]
[*]Impossible skill levels[/*]
[*]Unusual XP progression[/*]
[*]Suspicious mail, recipe and progression changes[/*]
[*]Mass object spawning[/*]
[*]Abnormally fast monster kills[/*]
[*]Impossible game-state values[/*]
[*]Suspicious daily luck changes[/*]
[/list]Because many of these checks happen on the [b]host[/b], they don't depend entirely on trusting information sent by the client.
[line]
[heading]🔍 Mod Verification[/heading]
When a player joins, Stardew Anti-Cheat can compare information from multiple sources:
[list]
[*]SMAPI's multiplayer mod handshake[/*]
[*]The Stardew Anti-Cheat client report[/*]
[*]Mod Unique IDs[/*]
[*]Mod versions[/*]
[*]Optional file fingerprints[/*]
[*]Periodic client status reports[/*]
[/list]The host can use several verification modes:
[b]ReportOnly[/b]
Detect and log problems without automatically punishing players.
[b]Blacklist[/b]
Flag configured prohibited mods.
[b]Whitelist[/b]
Allow only approved mods.
[b]Strict[/b]
Use stricter verification rules for controlled multiplayer environments.
For large private modpacks, the host can automatically create a whitelist from their currently installed mods using:
[code]ac_makewhitelist[/code]Use:
[code]ac_makewhitelist pin[/code]to also pin minimum versions.
[line]
[heading]📊 Suspicion Score[/heading]
Stardew Anti-Cheat uses a configurable [b]suspicion scoring system[/b] instead of treating every unusual event as proof of cheating.
Different violations can add different amounts of suspicion depending on their severity.
Suspicion can decay over time, helping reduce the impact of isolated false positives.
Depending on your configuration, the system can:
[list]
[*]Log the violation[/*]
[*]Notify the host[/*]
[*]Increase suspicion[/*]
[*]Disconnect the player[/*]
[*]Add the player to the local denylist[/*]
[*]Ban the player's platform account through Stardew Valley's multiplayer system[/*]
[/list]Automatic punishment is intentionally disabled by default.
The recommended approach is to run the mod in [b]ReportOnly[/b] mode first, review your logs, adjust thresholds for your modpack, and only then enable automatic enforcement.
[line]
[heading]🖥️ In-Game Host Panel[/heading]
Press [b]F9[/b] to open the anti-cheat interface.
The key can be changed in the configuration file.
For the host, the panel displays information such as:
[list]
[*]Connected players[/*]
[*]Verification status[/*]
[*]Suspicion score[/*]
[*]Current money[/*]
[*]Energy[/*]
[*]Inventory information[/*]
[*]Current location[/*]
[*]Tile position[/*]
[*]Skill levels[/*]
[*]Progress information[/*]
[*]Detected mods[/*]
[*]Recent violations[/*]
[/list]The host can also perform moderation actions directly from the panel, including:
[list]
[*]Approve a player[/*]
[*]Kick a player[/*]
[*]Add a player to the denylist[/*]
[*]Re-run verification[/*]
[*]Export security logs[/*]
[/list][line]
[heading]👤 Farmhand Status Panel[/heading]
Farmhands can also press [b]F9[/b].
Instead of seeing administrative information, they receive a read-only status screen showing their own anti-cheat connection.
It can show whether:
[list]
[*]Stardew Anti-Cheat loaded correctly[/*]
[*]The host requested verification[/*]
[*]Their mod list was submitted[/*]
[*]The host replied[/*]
[*]Periodic status updates are working[/*]
[*]Their current verification passed[/*]
[/list]Farmhands cannot see other players, host thresholds or moderation information.
[line]
[heading]📝 Detailed Security Logging[/heading]
Stardew Anti-Cheat can create detailed logs for investigation and troubleshooting.
Logs include information such as:
[list]
[*]Player connection events[/*]
[*]Verification results[/*]
[*]Detected violations[/*]
[*]Evidence associated with a violation[/*]
[*]Suspicion changes[/*]
[*]Enforcement actions[/*]
[*]Per-player activity[/*]
[/list]Logs are stored inside the Stardew Anti-Cheat mod folder.
Example structure:
[code]Mods/StardewAntiCheat/logs/[/code]including:
[code]security.log[/code]
General security and verification events.
[code]violations.log[/code]
Detected violations and their evidence.
[code]players/[/code]
Individual player logs.
[code]exports/[/code]
Exported log snapshots.
[line]
[heading]🧰 Host Console Commands[/heading]
Stardew Anti-Cheat includes several administrative commands.
[code]ac_status[/code]
Shows connected players, verification status and suspicion scores.
[code]ac_stats [player][/code]
Shows live player statistics.
[code]ac_player <player>[/code]
Displays detailed anti-cheat information about a player.
[code]ac_mods <player>[/code]
Displays detected mod information.
[code]ac_kick <player> [reason][/code]
Disconnects a player.
[code]ac_ban <player> [reason][/code]
Bans a player through Stardew Valley's multiplayer system.
[code]ac_deny <player>[/code]
Adds a player to the local denylist.
[code]ac_allow <id>[/code]
Removes an ID from the denylist.
[code]ac_denylist[/code]
Displays denylisted and banned players.
[code]ac_approve <player>[/code]
Manually approves a player and resets suspicion.
[code]ac_score <player> <value>[/code]
Changes a player's suspicion score.
[code]ac_makewhitelist [pin][/code]
Creates a mod whitelist from the host's installed mods.
[code]ac_fingerprints[/code]
Displays local mod fingerprints.
[code]ac_reload[/code]
Re-runs verification for connected players.
[code]ac_export[/code]
Exports security logs.
[code]ac_panel[/code]
Opens the in-game anti-cheat panel.
[line]
📥 Installation
[heading]Requirements[/heading]
[list]
[*][b]Stardew Valley 1.6.x[/b][/*]
[*][b]SMAPI 4.0.0 or newer[/b][/*]
[/list]The current version has been developed against Stardew Valley 1.6 and SMAPI 4.x.
No Harmony installation or additional runtime mod dependency is required.
[line]
[heading]Installing the Mod[/heading]
[list=1]
[*]Install the latest compatible version of [b]SMAPI[/b].[/*]
[*]Download Stardew Anti-Cheat.[/*]
[*]Extract the
[code]StardewAntiCheat[/code]folder into:[/*]
[/list][code]Stardew Valley/Mods/[/code][list=1]
[*]Launch the game through SMAPI.[/*]
[*]Load or create a multiplayer farm.[/*]
[*]The mod will automatically determine whether the current player is the host or a farmhand.[/*]
[*]Run the game once to generate
[code]config.json[/code].[/*]
[/list]For the complete verification system, Stardew Anti-Cheat should be installed by both the [b]host and farmhands[/b].
Some host-side behavioral checks can still work when a client doesn't have the mod installed, but client verification will contain less information.
[line]
⚙️ Recommended First-Time Configuration
Stardew Anti-Cheat defaults to a monitoring-focused configuration.
For a new installation, it is strongly recommended to:
[list=1]
[*]Keep verification in [b]ReportOnly[/b] mode.[/*]
[*]Keep automatic kicking and banning disabled.[/*]
[*]Play normally with your multiplayer group.[/*]
[*]Review
[code]logs/violations.log[/code].[/*]
[*]Adjust thresholds for your specific modpack.[/*]
[*]Enable enforcement only after you are comfortable with the results.[/*]
[/list]Highly modded games can legitimately produce behavior that looks unusual compared with vanilla Stardew Valley, so configuration is important.
[line]
🔐 Whitelist Mode for Private Modpacks
If everyone on your server should use the same approved modpack, [b]Whitelist mode[/b] is the recommended option.
Instead of manually entering every mod, run:
[code]ac_makewhitelist[/code]Stardew Anti-Cheat will generate the configuration using the mods currently installed on the host.
Then change the verification mode to:
[code]Whitelist[/code]This makes it much easier to maintain controlled private modpacks.
[line]
⚠️ Important Limitations
Stardew Anti-Cheat is designed to be transparent about what it can and cannot detect.
Infinite Health
A farmhand's health is not normally synchronized to the host in a way that provides reliable host-side validation.
Because of this, [b]infinite health cannot be reliably detected[/b].
Energy, however, is synchronized and can be validated.
Shared Money
When the farm uses a shared wallet, multiple players can modify the same synchronized money value.
The anti-cheat can detect suspicious changes, but attribution to one specific player may not always be reliable.
Separate wallets provide better attribution.
Combat
Stardew Valley does not provide the host with a complete synchronized history of every attack and damage event.
Combat detection therefore relies on indirect signals and should be considered less reliable than money or inventory validation.
Client-Side Mod Information
A sufficiently modified client can potentially falsify information it sends.
For that reason, client-reported mod lists and hashes should not be treated as cryptographic proof.
The strongest protections are the checks based on game state observed directly by the host.
The Host Is Trusted
The host is the authority in Stardew Valley multiplayer.
Stardew Anti-Cheat is designed to moderate [b]farmhands[/b], not to prevent the host from modifying their own game.
[line]
🔒 Privacy
Stardew Anti-Cheat does not need to upload player data to an external service.
Security information is stored locally by the host.
Depending on configuration, logs may contain:
[list]
[*]In-game farmer name[/*]
[*]Multiplayer ID[/*]
[*]Platform account ID when available[/*]
[*]Detected mod information[/*]
[*]Evidence associated with violations[/*]
[/list]Player names can also be excluded from logging through configuration.
Optional trainer/process detection is disabled by default. If enabled, it is intended only to compare configured suspicious process names; it is not designed to transmit a player's complete process list.
[line]
🎯 What This Mod Is For
Stardew Anti-Cheat is primarily intended for:
[list]
[*]Private multiplayer servers[/*]
[*]Community farms[/*]
[*]Controlled modpacks[/*]
[*]Multiplayer events[/*]
[*]Servers where the host wants moderation tools[/*]
[*]Groups that want visibility into suspicious behavior[/*]
[/list]It is [b]not[/b] intended to turn Stardew Valley into a perfectly secure competitive game.
Its purpose is to give the host better information, better logging and better tools while making common forms of cheating considerably more difficult to hide.
[line]

[b]Stardew Valley:[/b] 1.6.x
